Our reduction is from BDD, whose candidate solutions can be compared in polynomial time. Assume the reduction finds the optimal solution in one case among polynomially many, but that we do not know which one. Then we may call the reduction this polynomially many times, and keep a best solution among the returned ones. Concretely, our reduction will be ICALP 2016 proved correct if we know a tight approximation to λ1 (L(B)) and dist(t, L(B)), where (B, t) is the BDD instance. We can assume without loss of generality that we have these tight approximations, as the interval [1, 2n/2 ) may be covered by polynomially many intervals of the form x · [1, 1/(1 − 1/n)) for well-chosen rational x’s.
